passage: An ecosystem consists of biotic components like plants and animals, and abiotic factors such as sunlight, temperature, and water. Plants are producers that capture solar energy to create food, while consumers rely on these producers. Energy flows through trophic levels in a one-way direction, decreasing significantly at each step according to the ten percent law. Unlike nutrients, which cycle through the environment, energy is lost as heat and cannot be recycled. Decomposers are essential members of the food chain as they break down organic waste, returning nutrients to the soil. However, some non-biodegradable substances, like certain pesticides, do not break down. Instead, they accumulate in the tissues of organisms, increasing in concentration at higher trophic levels, a process known as biological magnification. This means top predators often carry the highest concentration of toxins, not because they are large, but because they consume many organisms from lower levels. Furthermore, the ozone layer in the stratosphere protects life by absorbing harmful ultraviolet radiation. It is not a physical hole in the sky, but a region where ozone gas concentration is depleted. Proper waste management is crucial, as burying waste in landfills does not eliminate environmental risks, and burning plastic releases toxic chemicals rather than making it biodegradable.

items.evidence: Unlike nutrients, which cycle through the environment, energy is lost as heat and cannot be recycled.
items.q: A farmer says the sun's energy used by a crop can be reused by the next crop. Is he right?
options: No, energy is lost as heat, so it cannot return
No, only the soil can store energy for reuse
No, energy cycles but only through the producers
No, plants lose energy only when they are cut
items.explain: Energy is lost as heat and cannot be recycled, unlike nutrients, which cycle through the environment.

wrong.why: thinks plants and soil hold energy for reuse
picks a nearby idea, that harvesting causes the loss

items.evidence: Decomposers are essential members of the food chain as they break down organic waste, returning nutrients to the soil.
items.q: If all decomposers in a forest disappeared, what would most likely happen to its soil?
options: Dead matter would pile up and nutrients would not return
Dead matter would vanish and nutrients would increase
Only the animals eating decomposers would be affected
Sunlight would stop reaching the plants growing there
items.explain: Decomposers break down organic waste and return nutrients, so without them waste piles up and soil loses nutrients.

wrong.why: thinks decomposers play no part in the food chain
thinks only the eater of the removed species is affected
mixes up sunlight, an abiotic factor, with the biotic cause

items.evidence: This means top predators often carry the highest concentration of toxins, not because they are large, but because they consume many organisms from lower levels.
items.q: Why does an eagle at the top of a food chain hold the most pesticide?
options: It eats many organisms that already carry pesticide
It grows bigger than every animal below it
It is the strongest, so it keeps more energy
It cannot pass any pesticide out as waste
items.explain: Top predators eat many lower organisms, each carrying toxins, so the toxins add up in their bodies.

wrong.why: thinks magnification means growing physically larger
thinks top predators hold the most energy
thinks toxins are excreted, not accumulated

items.evidence: It is not a physical hole in the sky, but a region where ozone gas concentration is depleted.
items.q: Scientists speak of a hole in the ozone layer. What does this hole really mean?
options: A region where ozone gas has become thinner
A gap in the sky where no air exists
A tear that lets in extra heat directly
A patch of stratosphere with no sunlight
items.explain: It is not a physical hole; it is a region where ozone gas concentration is depleted.

wrong.why: thinks it is a physical hole with no air
thinks the hole mainly lets in heat
confuses ozone depletion with a lack of sunlight

items.evidence: Proper waste management is crucial, as burying waste in landfills does not eliminate environmental risks, and burning plastic releases toxic chemicals rather than making it biodegradable.
items.q: A town burns its plastic waste to be safe. Which statement explains why this is a poor idea?
options: Burning gives off toxic chemicals and leaves plastic non-degradable
Burning turns plastic into ash that nature can break down
Burning is useless since burying removes all the risk
Burning makes plastic biodegradable but wastes useful energy
items.explain: Burning plastic releases toxic chemicals; it does not make plastic biodegradable, and landfills are not a safe fix.

wrong.why: thinks burning makes plastic natural ash
thinks buried waste is no longer a problem
half-accepts burning and invents an energy argument
